title: Ochre Health - Contract extension & regional acceleration
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-21
Time: 14:00 - 14:56 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Dr. Mira Patel (Ochre Head of ML), Jonas Reed (Ochre Platform Lead), Aisha Khan (Ochre Procurement)

Auto-summary: Customer wants to extend contract for 12 months, add capacity for a symptom-check product launch, test EU private cluster for data residency, and pilot APAC region. Security requirements call out KMS, SOC2 evidence, SSO. Redwood to run EU benchmark and provide pricing amendment.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Mira, Jonas, Aisha, great to see you again. We put 60 minutes on the cal to walk through the renewal plus the capacity and region pilot ask. Quick round robin — Ethan is our SE who will run the benchmark and lead the private pilot tech work.

[00:18] Dr. Mira Patel: Thanks Sofia. Yep. We're tight on time, so short context — our teletriage flow is moving to prod Q3, expected 2x token volume during peak. We need a contract extension and predictable capacity, plus strict EU residency for certain patient data. Also exploring APAC to improve latency for our Singapore customers.

[00:37] Ethan Cole: Great, Mira. Quick clarifying question — when you say 2x token volume, is that sustained or burst? And what's your current p50/p95?

[00:45] Jonas Reed: It's a mix. Sustained increase during working hours and big bursts overnight. Current average is about 120 RPS, p50 ~ 210ms, p95 ~ 780ms for our current model calls, token lengths average 320 tokens per request. We can send a CSV after this.

[01:12] Sofia Martinez: That's helpful. From a contract perspective, we typically handle this two ways: reserved Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-premise) for residency. We can combine reserved GPU pools with private control plane for EU. Both support canaries and rollouts. Cost and latency tradeoffs differ though.

[01:40] Dr. Mira Patel: For EU we need customer-managed KMS, audit logs for each inference, and SOC2 evidence. We can't have model data leaving EU without encryption and explicit MFA for keys.

[01:55] Ethan Cole: Understood. We support KMS integration and HSM-backed keys for private deployments. The audit logging is configurable — we can push per-token metadata to your SIEM or S3 within the EU boundary. Small note: there might be some field names in our logs that are redacted by default; we'll show the schema.

[02:22] Aisha Khan: From procurement, timeline is sensitive. We want amendment in place by mid-July to align with budgets, and the PO signed shortly after. Also need an estimate for incremental cost for 2x sustained and burst headroom.

[02:37] Sofia Martinez: Ok — high level pricing guidance now: reserved capacity for your forecasted sustained load with a 20% burst buffer typically optimizes cost. For private EU pilot there's an onboarding fee and slightly different unit economics because of dedicated infra. I'll send a draft amendment by Friday.

[03:05] Jonas Reed: On the technical side, for APAC we care about p50 less than 250ms on inference. Is that realistic with Dedicated in APAC versus routing to hosted?

[03:20] Ethan Cole: Two levers: deploy model nearer to users (APAC geocluster) and reduce cold-start/kv cache misses. For p50 250ms on typical 320-token requests, that pushes toward a local Dedicated node or edge private deployment. Hosted can sometimes meet that, but with variability. We can show historical latency profiles from similar customers.

[03:45] Dr. Mira Patel: Also we need to understand quantization implications on output fidelity. We can't degrade triage safety scenarios.

[03:55] Ethan Cole: Absolutely — we'll run A/B with quantized and fp16 configs in the benchmark and include a small eval suite (your golden prompts) to measure regression. We'll surface quality metrics alongside latency and cost.

[04:15] Sofia Martinez: Good — so proposed plan: 1) Redwood runs 2-week EU private benchmark using your payloads; 2) produce a readout with p50/p95, token cost delta, and quality regressions; 3) we propose amendment with capacity uplift and APAC pilot terms.

[04:35] Jonas Reed: Two things: our infra team needs the exact test harness (scripts, load profile) and an IAM account to provision test keys. Also we use Azure EU Central for storage, so any cross-region egress must be measured.

[04:52] Ethan Cole: We'll provide the harness and a terraform snippet for provisioning service accounts in your VPC. For the test keys, we can use temporary keys or integrate with your KMS. We'll try to keep all storage inside EU to avoid egress.

[05:12] Aisha Khan: On the amendment — will there be an SLA change for dedicated + private? We require 99.9% uptime for production endpoints in our contract.

[05:23] Sofia Martinez: For reserved Dedicated we have SLA tiers; 99.9% is typical for Dedicated with operational support tier. For Private there are options — if you choose Redwood-managed private control plane with our premium ops add-on, we can meet similar targets and provide incident runbooks. We'll include SLA language in the draft.

[05:40] Dr. Mira Patel: One more security point — need proof of SOC2 Type II report and details on RBAC. Also an audit trail of key usage.

[05:52] Ethan Cole: We'll attach SOC2 docs and an RBAC guide. Key usage logs can be exported to your SIEM with timestamps and request ids. There may be some noise in field mappings — we'll map to your schema during the pilot.

[06:10] Sofia Martinez: Quick competitive note — you mentioned MajorCloudAI in the RFP. How do we stack up?

[06:18] Jonas Reed: MajorCloudAI offered cheaper hosted rates but couldn't promise EU private with HSM at the price point. LMServeCo did a private deployment but quoting timeline was 8-12 weeks.

[06:30] Sofia Martinez: Right — our angle is unified inference across environments and faster onboarding for private pilots. We'll show a cost/lantency matrix in the amendment.

[06:45] Ethan Cole: For the benchmark, I'll include two runs: quantized low-cost and full precision. We'll also test batching and prefix caching — those often move the needle substantially for cost without hurting latency for median requests.

[07:03] Dr. Mira Patel: That sounds good. One small ask — can you capture per-route token accounting so we can map costs to product lines?

[07:12] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we have token-level breakdowns per route in the Console; we'll include an example CSV in the readout.

[07:25] Jonas Reed: Regarding APAC pilot — what's the minimal footprint we need to spin up for meaningful p50 measurement?

[07:33] Ethan Cole: Usually a single geocluster node with 4-8 GPUs depending on model size, plus a small reserved pool for warm KV cache. For your expected peak we'd start with a modest pool and scale up if the benchmark shows headroom issues.

[07:50] Aisha Khan: Procurement needs a cost delta for the next board meeting (July 8). Is that feasible?

[07:58] Sofia Martinez: We'll aim to get a draft amendment and high-level cost delta by June 25 so you can use it in prep for July 8. The benchmark readout will follow the two-week run which completes around July 12 if started early July.

[08:16] Dr. Mira Patel: One minor note — for the eval suite, we'll include safety-critical prompts; we'll need the output redaction and retention policies spelled out.

[08:28] Ethan Cole: We'll document retention windows and redaction options. For Private deployments we can set retention to zero for transient KV caches and only persist explicit logs per your policy.

[08:45] Sofia Martinez: Great. Let's do a quick recap and owners. Ethan — you run the benchmark and share harness by Monday (June 28). Sofia — price amendment by June 25. Jonas — send token and latency CSV by June 23. Aisha — confirm PO timeline by June 30.

[09:05] Jonas Reed: We'll get the CSV and a short tech spec over to Ethan today.

[09:12] Aisha Khan: Procurement will confirm internal approval flows — expect reply by June 30.

[09:18] Dr. Mira Patel: OK thanks everyone. Looking forward to the benchmark — our chance to validate the EU private path.

[09:25] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all. We'll follow up with meeting notes and links to the SOC2 pack, benchmark harness, and the draft amendment. Any final questions?

[09:33] Jonas Reed: One last — will we get a contact for SRE during the pilot?

[09:36] Ethan Cole: Yes — I'll assign an SRE and include their on-call calendar in the harness repo.

[09:42] Sofia Martinez: Perfect. We'll send calendar invite for a technical kickoff once Ethan posts the harness. Thanks, everyone. End call.

(Transcript ends — automated engine notes: some speaker labels may be approximate; minor transcription errors possible, proper nouns for internal Redwood products may be imperfect.)
